# Shipyard

**A shared library of opinionated AI agent skills — write once, run identically in Claude Code and Codex.**

Shipyard is published as [`@symbtech/shipyard`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@symbtech/shipyard) on npm. Installing it drops a full set of skills, project instruction files, and a prompt library into your project, so every agent your team uses follows the same process — from scoping a request, to shipping it, to reviewing the branch.

## Why Shipyard

Claude Code and Codex each load "skills" their own way, and teams tend to end up rewriting the same process instructions twice, or drifting out of sync between tools. Shipyard fixes that by maintaining **one canonical copy of each skill** and generating the tool-specific adapter from it, so:

- Claude Code and Codex both run the exact same instructions.
- Fixing or improving a skill happens in one file, not two.
- `npx shipyard` installs (or updates) the whole bundle into any project in one step, without ever overwriting a file you've customized.

## Quick Start

```bash
npm install @symbtech/shipyard
npx shipyard
```

`npm install` triggers a `postinstall` hook that copies everything into your project root automatically; run `npx shipyard` afterward to confirm it landed (or to copy it manually if the hook was blocked — see [Installing](#installing)). Skip to [How It Works](#how-it-works) to see what you got, or to [The Skills](#the-skills) to start using it.

### Starting a brand-new project without installing anything

If there's no project yet, don't use `npm install` — that copies the entire 16-skill bundle into a repo that doesn't exist. Instead:

```bash
# Scaffold into a new subdirectory, auto-detect claude/codex on PATH
npx @symbtech/shipyard scaffold ./my-new-app

# Scaffold into the current directory (target-dir defaults to ".")
mkdir my-new-app && cd my-new-app
npx @symbtech/shipyard scaffold

# Force Claude Code even if codex is also installed
npx @symbtech/shipyard scaffold ./my-new-app --tool claude

# Force Codex
npx @symbtech/shipyard scaffold ./my-new-app --tool codex

# --tool= works too
npx @symbtech/shipyard scaffold ./billing-service --tool=codex

# Absolute path target
npx @symbtech/shipyard scaffold /Users/username/Desktop/Projects/billing-service
```

This runs the `scaffold` skill directly: it reads `SKILL.md` and its guides from the package `npx` fetched (never from your project), builds a prompt from them, and launches `claude` or `codex` — whichever it finds on `PATH` — in `./my-new-app` (created if missing) so you can answer the usual scaffold questions interactively. Nothing shipyard-specific is ever written to the target directory: no `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `prompt-library/` — only the scaffolded project itself. Pass `--tool claude` or `--tool codex` to force one over the other.

Once the project exists, run `npm install @symbtech/shipyard` inside it as usual to bring in the full skill set for everything downstream (`dock`, `intent`, etc.).

## How It Works

Every skill is written once under `.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` — the canonical, tool-agnostic instructions. The Claude Code and Codex copies are thin adapters that just point back at that single source of truth:

```text
.agents/skills/blueprint/SKILL.md   ← canonical instructions live here
.claude/skills/blueprint/SKILL.md   ← thin pointer: "read .agents/... and follow it"
.codex/skills/blueprint/SKILL.md    ← thin pointer: "read .agents/... and follow it"
```

- **Claude Code** reads `.claude/skills/`, invoked with `/<skill-name>`.
- **Codex** reads `.codex/skills/`, invoked by naming the skill in a prompt. Each Codex skill also ships an `agents/openai.yaml` manifest (`display_name`, `short_description`, `default_prompt`) alongside its `SKILL.md`, for registering the same skill with OpenAI-style agent/GPT builders — Claude Code doesn't need this, so it isn't duplicated there.

Whichever tool an engineer opens, the underlying behavior — what questions get asked, what files get written, when a skill hands off to the next one — is identical, because it's the same `SKILL.md`.

Skill names are short (`implement`, `intent`, `secure`, …) since `@symbtech/shipyard` is already the namespace — no per-skill prefix needed. Each skill's frontmatter also carries a stable `id: shipyard:<skill-name>` (e.g. `shipyard:implement`), so anything that needs a collision-proof, version-stable reference has one, even though invocation always uses the short name.

## What Gets Installed

Installing Shipyard adds the current setup bundle to your project root:

```text
.agents/
  skills/
    intent/                    blueprint/                     worklist/
    implement/                 branch-review/                 md-to-pdf/
    dock/                      bughunt/                        scaffold/
    handoff/                   secure/                        optimize-performance/
    codebase-design/           domain-modeling/               grilling/
    improve-codebase-architecture/
.claude/
  skills/
    <same 16 skills>/SKILL.md        (pointer into .agents/)
.codex/
  skills/
    <same 16 skills>/SKILL.md        (pointer into .agents/)
    <same 16 skills>/agents/openai.yaml  (OpenAI agent/GPT manifest)
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md
prompt-library/
  README.md
```

- `.agents/skills/` — the full instructions for every skill, plus any reference files, templates, and scripts each one needs (e.g. `branch-review`'s report template, `md-to-pdf`'s conversion script).
- `.claude/skills/` and `.codex/skills/` — thin per-tool pointers, so each tool loads the same instructions without duplicating them.
- `AGENTS.md` — the project-level instruction file used by Codex-style agents.
- `CLAUDE.md` — the project-level instruction file used by Claude Code.
- `prompt-library/README.md` — reusable, copy-pasteable prompts for every skill and workflow below.

The setup command is **additive**: it creates missing files and skips anything that already exists, so it's always safe to re-run after an update.

## The Skills

| Skill | What it does | Invocation | Produces |
|---|---|---|---|
| `intent` | Calibrates how much clarification a request needs (zero questions to an open-ended discussion), then confirms scope before anything is built. | Explicit only | `.shipyard/work/<name>/context.md` |
| `blueprint` | Turns a confirmed `context.md` into an implementation-ready spec, grounded in the codebase. | Explicit only | `.shipyard/work/<name>/spec.md` |
| `worklist` | Decomposes an approved spec into an ordered **tracer bullet** worklist — thin, end-to-end slices instead of layer-by-layer tasks. | Explicit only | `.shipyard/work/<name>/worklist.md` |
| `implement` | Burns down a tracer-bullet worklist one bullet at a time, with tests, verification, and explicit human approval before continuing. | Auto-invoked | Updates `worklist.md` in place; final Summary/Test-plan/JIRA handoff |
| `branch-review` | Reviews a source branch against a target branch and writes a findings-first merge-readiness report. | Auto-invoked | `.shipyard/branch-review-<source>-into-<target>.md` |
| `md-to-pdf` | Converts a Markdown file into a PDF, preferring `pandoc`/`mdpdf`/`wkhtmltopdf` and falling back to a built-in renderer. | Auto-invoked | A `.pdf` file |
| `dock` | Surveys a repository and writes a grounded AI knowledge base: eight files plus a `context.md` digest, all under `.shipyard/`. | Explicit only | `.shipyard/*.md` + `.shipyard/context.md` |
| `bughunt` | Triages first — fixes an obvious, visible-cause bug directly; otherwise a reproduce-first discipline for hard bugs and performance regressions: build a tight, red-capable test loop before hypothesizing. | Auto-invoked | A regression test + fix |
| `scaffold` | Bootstraps a brand-new project end to end — project type, org technology guide, requirements, scaffolded skeleton. | Auto-invoked | A new project skeleton on disk |
| `handoff` | Compacts the current conversation into a cold-start document for a fresh agent, linking out to any spec/worklist/ADR already on disk instead of restating them. | Explicit only | `.shipyard/handoff/<topic-slug>-<date>.md` |
| `secure` | Threat-models trust boundaries before hardening code — input handling, auth, data storage, uploads, external integrations, dependencies, and LLM features — against OWASP-class vulnerabilities. | Auto-invoked | Hardened code in place |
| `optimize-performance` | Measures a baseline, identifies the real bottleneck, applies one fix, and re-measures before keeping or reverting it — frontend, backend, queries, and databases. | Auto-invoked | A measured, verified fix, kept or reverted, logged in an attempt ledger |
| `codebase-design` | Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules — module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality — plus the deletion test and the design-it-twice parallel sub-agent pattern. | Auto-invoked | Prose recommendations; no files |
| `domain-modeling` | Actively builds and sharpens a project's domain model — challenges fuzzy terms, stress-tests scenarios, and writes `CONTEXT.md`/ADRs the moment a term or decision crystallises. | Auto-invoked | `CONTEXT.md`, `CONTEXT-MAP.md`, `docs/adr/*.md` |
| `grilling` | Pressure-tests one already-chosen decision with a single sharp question at a time — constraints, dependencies, shape, what's hidden, what survives — then hands back the confirmed shape. | Explicit only | Prose confirmation; no files |
| `improve-codebase-architecture` | Scans a codebase for deepening opportunities, presents them as a visual HTML report, then grills through whichever candidate is picked. | Explicit only | A temp-dir HTML report; hands off to `grilling` |

"Explicit only" skills (`disable-model-invocation: true`) never fire from a plain description match — name them directly (`/intent` in Claude Code, `Use $intent to ...` in Codex). The rest auto-trigger when a request matches their description, but can always be named explicitly too.

## Recommended Build Workflow

For building a feature end to end, the skills chain in this order, each handing off to the next:

```text
intent → blueprint → worklist → implement → branch-review → md-to-pdf
```

1. **intent** — clarify the request and confirm scope; logs `.shipyard/work/<name>/context.md`.
2. **blueprint** — turn the confirmed context into `.shipyard/work/<name>/spec.md`.
3. **worklist** — decompose the spec into `.shipyard/work/<name>/worklist.md`, a set of ordered tracer bullets.
4. **implement** — implement the worklist one tracer bullet at a time, stopping for approval after each.
5. **branch-review** — once the branch is ready, review it against the target branch and write a Markdown report.
6. **md-to-pdf** — optionally convert that report into a shareable PDF.

Each step only hands off when you're ready — none of these skills starts the next step on its own. See [`prompt-library/README.md`](setup/prompt-library/README.md) for copy-pasteable prompts covering this entire chain, in both Claude Code and Codex form.

A second chain covers architecture reviews, separate from the feature-build chain above:

```text
improve-codebase-architecture → grilling
```

1. **improve-codebase-architecture** — scans for deepening opportunities (using `codebase-design`'s vocabulary) and writes a visual HTML report to a temp file.
2. **grilling** — once a candidate is picked, pressure-tests it one question at a time until its constraints, dependencies, shape, and surviving tests are locked in.

`domain-modeling` runs alongside both chains rather than at a fixed step — it fires whenever a term needs sharpening or a decision needs recording in `CONTEXT.md`/`docs/adr/`.

## Dock the Repo First

Run `dock` once up front (and again after major changes) to build a grounded knowledge base under `.shipyard/` plus a `.shipyard/context.md` digest. Every skill above checks for that knowledge base first and reads it instead of re-auditing the repository from scratch:

- `intent` skims `.shipyard/context.md` before asking questions.
- `blueprint` and `worklist` ground themselves in `.shipyard/architecture.md`, `.shipyard/coding-conventions.md`, `.shipyard/decisions.md`.
- `implement` checks `.shipyard/coding-conventions.md`/`.shipyard/api.md` for conventions to follow.
- `branch-review` checks the diff against `.shipyard/architecture.md`/`.shipyard/decisions.md`.

None of them override what `dock` wrote — they only read it, falling back to a direct repo audit for anything it doesn't cover, or if it doesn't exist yet. `scaffold` suggests running `dock` right after scaffolding a brand-new project, so the knowledge base exists from day one.

## Where Files Land

Everything Shipyard produces lives under `.shipyard/` and is indexed from `.shipyard/README.md` — that index file links to every knowledge-base file, every work item, and every branch-review report, so nothing it generates has to be found by searching the directory by hand.

| Path | Written by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `.shipyard/README.md` | Every skill below, on first write and every update | Index of everything Shipyard has generated |
| `.shipyard/work/<name>/context.md` | `intent` | Confirmed scope for one piece of work |
| `.shipyard/work/<name>/spec.md` | `blueprint` | Implementation-ready spec |
| `.shipyard/work/<name>/worklist.md` | `worklist`, updated by `implement` | Tracer-bullet plan and progress |
| `.shipyard/architecture.md`, `project-overview.md`, `business-domain.md`, `coding-conventions.md`, `api.md`, `glossary.md`, `decisions.md`, `setup.md` | `dock` | Full-depth AI knowledge base |
| `.shipyard/context.md` | `dock` | Concise digest linking into the rest of `.shipyard/` |
| `.shipyard/branch-review-<source>-into-<target>.md` | `branch-review` | Merge-readiness report |
| `.shipyard/handoff/<topic-slug>-<date>.md` | `handoff` | Cold-start doc for a fresh agent picking up the work |

`<name>` is a short kebab-case slug for the task, chosen the first time `intent` or `blueprint` runs, and reused by every later step in that same piece of work.

## Prompt Library

Installed at `prompt-library/README.md`, it contains ready-to-use, copy-pasteable prompts for every skill and workflow above — each with a placeholder-filled prompt for Codex/general agents *and* a Claude Code slash-command equivalent. Copy a prompt, replace values like `<source-branch>` or `<report-md>`, and paste it into whichever tool you're using.

## Installing

Run this from the project you want to set up:

```bash
npm install @symbtech/shipyard
```

The package runs its setup script after installation and copies setup files into the project where `npm install` was started.

With npm 12+, dependency install scripts may be blocked by default. If npm reports that `@symbtech/shipyard` was blocked, approve and rebuild it:

```bash
npm install-scripts approve @symbtech/shipyard
npm rebuild @symbtech/shipyard
```

You can also run the setup command manually at any time (e.g. to pick up files added by a newer version):

```bash
npx shipyard
```

## Setup Behavior

The setup command copies these package directories when they exist:

- `setup/` into the project root
- `skills/` into `skills/`
- `prompt-library/` into `prompt-library/`

Files are copied only when the target path does not already exist — existing project files are always preserved. Example output:

```text
@symbtech/shipyard setup copied 27 files to /path/to/project.
@symbtech/shipyard setup skipped 2 existing files.
```

## Package Contents

The npm package includes:

- `setup/`
  - `.agents/skills/` — canonical skill instructions
  - `.claude/skills/` — Claude Code adapters
  - `.codex/skills/` — Codex adapters + OpenAI agent manifests
  - `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`
  - `prompt-library/`
- `scripts/`
- `README.md`

The package metadata also reserves top-level `skills/` and `prompt-library/` as published paths for future bundles. The setup script safely skips any package source directory that isn't present.

## Commands

```bash
npx shipyard
```

Copies missing setup assets into the current project.

```bash
npx @symbtech/shipyard scaffold [target-dir] [--tool claude|codex]
```

Runs the `scaffold` skill against `target-dir` (default: current directory) without installing the package into it — see [Starting a brand-new project without installing anything](#starting-a-brand-new-project-without-installing-anything). Auto-detects `claude`/`codex` on `PATH` unless `--tool` is given.

```bash
npm run build:lib
```

Builds a local `dist/` bundle (and `dist/manifest.json` listing every discovered skill) from `skills/` and `prompt-library/` when present, plus `setup/` when present. This also runs automatically before publish, via `prepack`.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer
- npm, pnpm, or another package manager that can install npm packages

## Repository Development

Repository layout:

```text
scripts/
  setup-project.mjs      the `shipyard` CLI / postinstall hook
  build-lib.mjs           builds dist/ and dist/manifest.json
setup/                    everything published to consuming projects
  .agents/skills/
  .claude/skills/
  .codex/skills/
  AGENTS.md
  CLAUDE.md
  prompt-library/
.claude/skills/           this repo's own dev-only tooling (not published)
  shipyard-skill-builder/  reference for writing/editing skills well
package.json
bitbucket-pipelines.yml   publishes to npm on `v*` tags
README.md
```

To add or change a skill:

1. Edit the canonical instructions under `setup/.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` — this is the only copy that should ever contain real logic.
2. Keep `setup/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` and `setup/.codex/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` as thin pointers back to it (see any existing skill for the exact wording). Add an `agents/openai.yaml` manifest under the Codex copy only if the skill should be reachable from OpenAI-style agent/GPT builders — Claude Code doesn't read it, so don't duplicate it there.
3. If the skill hands off to another one, or is handed off to, say so explicitly in the prose — that's how the [Recommended Build Workflow](#recommended-build-workflow) stays coherent.
4. Add a matching entry to [`prompt-library/README.md`](setup/prompt-library/README.md) with both a Codex/general prompt and a Claude Code slash-command form.
5. Run `npm run build:lib` to confirm the skill is discovered and included in `dist/manifest.json`.

`.claude/skills/shipyard-skill-builder/` (repo root, not under `setup/`) is this project's own reference for writing skills well — invocation trade-offs, information hierarchy, and common failure modes to avoid. It's dev-only tooling and is never copied into consuming projects.

Publishing is automated: pushing a `v*` tag runs `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, which builds `dist/` and publishes to npm.
